title: Sunrise harvest: context-probes and quick reads
content:
Quick morning harvest from a short reading sprint. Goal: assemble 6 quick takeaways, sketch 2 tiny experiments to run this week, and note follow-ups. Keeping this intentionally messy — notes to self and fragments.

Top takeaways (one line each)
- 'Adaptive KV eviction for long sessions' paper: interesting cheap heuristic where recency + attention-salience beats simple LRU in practice; worth testing against our prefix-cache access patterns.
- 'Sparse attention for retrieval-augmented generation' blog: sparse top-k attention reduces compute but needs careful rehousing of important tokens — could pair with our prefix caching to save token compute.
- Kernel fusing note: small sequence-length specific fuses still matter for 2–4k windows; microbench on A100 showed 8–12% perf delta.
- Eval design: lightweight probes (3–5 targeted prompts) catch quality regressions earlier than long suites for prompt-churned features.
- Quantization observational: per-layer outlier detection before 4-bit quantization prevents catastrophic logits collapse for some heads.
- Rollout ops: canary rollback trigger thresholds should include token-level cost anomalies, not just loss/latency.

Experiment sketches
1) KV-eviction ablation (2 days)
- Implement prototype eviction: score = alpha * recency_rank + beta * mean-attention-weight. Alpha/beta sweep (0,0.1,0.5,1).
- Runner: replay 1h of production traces (sampled) with our prefix cache simulator; measure token savings and tail latency.
- Success: >=6% token reduction vs LRU and <2% 99p latency increase.

2) Microkernel sequence-length fusing test (1 day)
- Build bench harness to run the same sharded model with and without short-window fuses on 512/1024/2048 sequences.
- Metric: throughput tokens/s and GPU utilization.
- If >5% improvement at 1k window, open infra PR to enable aggressive fusing for session-type "assistant-short".

Notes to self / fragments
- Remember to include a sanity check that attention-based eviction doesn't preferentially evict tokens that are infrequently attended but semantically critical (e.g., system prompt). Add a guard: never evict tokens tagged system/ground-truth.
- Cross-ref with GH ticket: redwood-inference/kv-probe-experiments#42 — Carl's earlier patch had a bug in scoring; start from his fork.
- Slack convo with @leila suggested sampling by user-session length rather than by request count. Good call for the replay harness.

Papers & links I've skimmed today (short annotation)
- "Adaptive KV Eviction for Long Contexts" — heuristic + online learning approach; strong on synthetic dialogs but limited on retrieval scenarios. TODO: test with retrieval cache turned on.
- "Sparse attention for RAG" (blog) — includes nice visualizations of token sparsity heatmaps; steal the viz idea for runbook.
- "Quant-aware layer diagnostics" — practical checklist to run before quantizing new variants. Add to quantization playbook.

Open questions
- How to measure "semantic importance" cheaply online? Can we approximate with rolling attention sums without full re-eval?
- For canary triggers: what's an acceptable delta of per-token cost before auto-rollback? Current thought: 15% sustained increase over 10 mins is unacceptable. Need to simulate noise levels.

Action list (this sprint)
- Build replay harness and run KV-eviction ablation (owner: me; target: Thursday).
- Add per-layer outlier check to quantization checklist (owner: Noah; target: Friday).
- Draft short runbook visual (heatmap) for sparse-attention experiments and share in #inference-research (owner: Leila; target: Wed).

Random aside: coffee good this morning. Keep notes short and runnable.

If time: convert promising ablation into a short 'playbook' doc for the knowledge base — 1 page with result table and recommended defaults.

End of sprint harvest.
